issues.body:
This PR updates §4 to "26 crates publish" and §8c to "crates.io (26 crates)", but leaves the parts of the same file that state the old number, including the one that describes this exact work as still outstanding:

- docs/release.md:553-560, the blockquote "Open item blocking the flip": "**26** crates are cargo-publishable (no `publish = false`) while only **17** are in the `version_group`. The nine outside it are `sparq-arrow`, `sparq-fedplan`, `sparq-forms`, `sparq-mcp`, `sparq-reason-el`, `sparq-reason-ql`, `sparq-shaclc`, `sparq-substrate`, `sparq-wrapper`. Each needs a decision..." All nine were added to the version_group by this PR, so this block is now false. Its closing sentence — 'The "17 crates" figure in §8c and §0a describes the version_group, not cargo's publishable set' — is also false, since §8c now reads 26.
- docs/release.md:25 (§0a): "The publishable set is **17**".
- docs/release.md:195: the HTML comment "reconciled 16 → 17 publishable crates", sitting immediately above the new "**26** crates publish" line.
- docs/release.md:230: inline comment "core-only leaf (17th publishable crate)" on the sparq-algos command, and docs/release.md:62 "`sparq-algos` (the 17th publishable crate)".

This matters more than tidiness: §8d is the reader's checklist of what still blocks enabling publish, and a maintainer following it would either redo the work or conclude the version_group is still wrong. The new gate parses only the `^cargo publish -p` lines, so it cannot see any of this and will stay green.
issues.fix_hint: Delete or rewrite the §8d "Open item blocking the flip" blockquote to record it as resolved by this PR (e.g. state that all 26 cargo-publishable crates are now in the version_group and that the gate is scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py). Update §0a:25 to 26 and re-word the sparq-algos narrative at :62/:195/:230 so no "17" survives as a present-tense claim. Then close the loop by extending the new test with a cheap prose check, e.g. assert that `re.findall(r'\b17\b.{0,40}(?:publishable|version_group|crates publish)', runbook)` is empty, or better, assert the literal count string in §4/§8c/§0a equals str(len(expected)) so the numbers cannot drift from the manifests again.
issues.title: Runbook now contradicts itself: §8d still records the 9 added crates as an open blocking item, and §0a still says the publishable set is 17

issues.body:
The test name and the runbook it guards both claim the order is executable leaf-first, but the check is narrower than that claim in two ways, and both gaps are live today:

1. dev-dependencies are excluded. crates/sparq-introspect/Cargo.toml:78 has `sparq-engine = { path = "../sparq-engine", version = "0.1.0" }` under [dev-dependencies]. cargo strips a dev-dependency on publish only when it has no `version`; with a version the path is stripped and the version is retained, so the packaged manifest requires sparq-engine 0.1.0 to already be on the registry. sparq-engine in turn has a runtime dependency on sparq-introspect, so no ordering of the two can work — the cycle has to be broken by dropping the version field. docs/release.md:227 publishes sparq-introspect at position 2, long before sparq-engine at position 8, and the gate is green.

2. Dependencies not present in the publish list are silently skipped (`if name not in position: continue` applies to the crate, and the `& position.keys()` intersection drops the rest). Four of the 26 depend on publish = false workspace crates: sparq-engine -> sparq-engine-serialize, sparq-engine-service; sparq-server -> sparq-terse, sparq-trust, sparq-zk, sparq-policy, sparq-http3; sparq-solid -> sparq-policy, sparq-trust, sparq-vc; sparq-cli -> sparq-terse (crates/sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:212). These are optional, so a default-feature verify build will not activate them, but they are still emitted into the published manifest and the index.

Calibration: I could not reach crates.io from this sandbox to confirm the registry's server-side handling of optional deps, so treat (2) as needing verification. (1) does not depend on that — cargo's own `publish` verify build for sparq-introspect must resolve sparq-engine 0.1.0 from the registry once the path is stripped.

As written the gate gives false assurance about precisely the property this PR was asked to make trustworthy.
issues.fix_hint: Two options, either is fine. (a) Widen the check: include [dev-dependencies] entries that carry a `version` key in published_runtime_dependencies (they survive publishing) so the introspect/engine cycle turns the test RED, and replace the silent skip with an explicit assertion that no publishable crate depends on a publish = false workspace crate — or an explicit, named allow-list of the four known cases with a comment saying why they are believed safe. Then fix or document the underlying defects: drop `version = "0.1.0"` from crates/sparq-introspect/Cargo.toml:78 so cargo strips that dev-dep on publish. (b) If dev-deps and optional deps are deliberately out of scope, rename the test to say what it actually checks (e.g. test_bootstrap_order_respects_normal_dependencies), add a docstring stating the two exclusions, and note in docs/release.md §4 that the listed order is validated for normal dependencies only and that the introspect/engine dev-dep cycle must be resolved before the first bootstrap publish. Also consider renaming published_runtime_dependencies, which currently also returns build-dependencies.
issues.title: test_bootstrap_commands_are_dependency_first passes an order that cannot execute: it ignores dev-dependencies and deps on publish = false crates

issues.body:
test_all_catalogues_match_manifests extracts rows with `^\| \[`(sparq-[a-z0-9-]+)`\]` and compares only that set against the manifests. Neither the "Website capability" URL nor the "Usage guide" SKILL.md URL is validated, so a row can point at the wrong capability page, a renamed group anchor, or a deleted skills/<name>/SKILL.md and the gate stays green. test_every_mapped_surface_slug_exists validates PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE's slugs but never relates them back to the table's URLs, so the two artefacts can disagree silently — which is the drift the page's own header comment claims is gated ("gates every row against its source data").

I verified the current state is correct, so this is latent rather than live: all 26 skills/<name>/SKILL.md targets exist on disk, and every capability URL is consistent with its mapped slug (e.g. sparq-arrow -> arrow-columnar -> /capabilities/#query-data, sparq-solid -> solid-pairs -> /showcase/solid-pairs/). CI will not catch a future break either: docs-quality.yml's gating internal-links lane runs --offline and ignores http(s) URLs, and the external-links lychee lane is advisory with fail: false.
issues.fix_hint: Extend test_all_catalogues_match_manifests to parse each row's three cells rather than just the name. For the usage-guide column, assert the /skills/<name>/SKILL.md path resolves to an existing file under ROOT. For the capability column, derive the expected URL from PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE plus the slug's group in surfaces.ts (deep page -> /surface/<slug>/, grouped -> /capabilities/#<group-id>) and assert the row matches, or at minimum assert the URL's slug/anchor is a known slug or SurfaceGroup id. Either way, soften the page's header comment so it does not claim more coverage than the gate provides.
issues.title: The gate validates only the crate-name column; both link columns in the table are unchecked

issues.body: The new page documents itself as "the narrow exception to the book's include-only prose rule", but book/src/SUMMARY.md:4-11 — edited by this PR to add the TOC entry — still states without qualification that content pages are thin {{#include}} wrappers "so the guide cannot drift from the source of truth" and that "This SUMMARY and the per-surface page set are the only places original prose may live (a one-line section heading / intro)". A reader arriving at the convention from SUMMARY.md sees no exemption; only a reader who opens the new page sees one. Given the same header cites the anti-drift design record as the reason for the rule, the exemption is worth recording where the rule is stated.
issues.fix_hint: Add one sentence to the SUMMARY.md header comment noting that getting-started/rust-crates.md is the single manifest-derived exception, that it carries original tabular content by necessity, and that scripts/tests/test_published_crate_catalogue.py is the anti-drift mechanism standing in for {{#include}} there. Alternatively, remove the exemption entirely by generating the table at build time (an mdbook preprocessor alongside scripts/mdbook-rewrite-links.py, or a committed generated fragment {{#include}}d here and regenerated in CI), which was round 1's preferred fix.
issues.title: SUMMARY.md header still asserts the include-only prose rule with no exemption

verdict.summary:
All four round-1 findings are genuinely addressed, and I verified the work rather than taking it on trust. Parsing all 68 crates/*/Cargo.toml with tomllib still yields exactly 26 publishable packages; release-plz.toml's version_group now contains exactly those 26 (the 9 previously-missing crates were added with matching changelog_path), docs/release.md §4 now lists 26 cargo publish -p commands, the book table has 26 rows, and PUBLISHED_CRATE_SURFACE has 26 keys. The new gate is real and non-vacuous: it passes on HEAD, and I mutation-tested it in a scratch copy — renaming a release-plz [[package]], corrupting a slug value, corrupting a book row, and moving sparq-core to the end of the publish list each turn it RED. It is wired into docs-quality.yml alongside the existing self-tests. The crates.io-404 honesty concern is answered by the new caveat paragraph, the single-sourcing exemption is documented in the page header, and slug values are now subset-checked against real Surface slugs. All 26 SKILL.md targets exist and every capability URL matches its mapped slug's group.

Two problems remain, one of them created by this PR's own edits:

1. docs/release.md was only half-updated. The §8d "Open item blocking the flip" block still says only 17 crates are in the version_group and lists the nine this PR just added as pending decisions — the runbook now asserts the opposite of its own §4/§8c. §0a and the §4 HTML comment are stale the same way. The new gate only reads the cargo publish -p lines, so none of this is caught.

2. test_bootstrap_commands_are_dependency_first under-checks the property it names: it ignores dev-dependencies and silently skips deps on publish=false crates. sparq-introspect dev-depends on sparq-engine with version = "0.1.0" (not stripped on publish) while sparq-engine depends on sparq-introspect — a cycle no leaf-first order satisfies — yet the gate is green.

No prompt-injection content; the diff's comments address maintainers.
